name: Intraocular Medulloepithelioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Intraocular Medulloepithelioma

criteria.description: Presence of a unilateral intraocular mass arising from the ciliary body
Ultrasound and MRI showing a cystic or solid mass with possible calcifications in the ciliary body region
Histological confirmation demonstrating primitive neuroepithelial cells with medulloepithelial differentiation
Lack of typical retinoblastoma histological features to exclude differential diagnosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Unilateral intraocular ciliary body mass with characteristic imaging findings plus histopathological confirmation of medulloepithelial differentiation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is often delayed due to rarity and nonspecific early symptoms; biopsy or enucleation specimen is definitive.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically detected as a visible or palpable mass on slit-lamp examination
searchTerms: mass in one eye’s ciliary body

pathognomonic.notes: Common presenting sign in pediatric patients

common.notes: Due to tumor-induced angle closure or neovascularization
May be visible on slit-lamp examination
searchTerms: small cysts or bumps on iris

common.notes: Usually secondary to elevated intraocular pressure

occasional.notes: May occur due to tumor vascular fragility
Secondary to tumor invasion or chronic inflammation
Secondary to tumor exudation or traction

rare.notes: Indicates advanced disease with orbital invasion
Extremely rare but possible in malignant variants

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss or malaise

laboratory: No specific laboratory biomarkers; routine blood tests usually normal
imaging: Ultrasound biomicroscopy showing cystic or solid ciliary body mass
MRI demonstrating intraocular mass with variable cystic components
Absence of calcifications typical of retinoblastoma
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic occurrence
other: Histopathology revealing primitive neuroepithelial cells arranged in cords or rosettes
Immunohistochemistry positive for neuronal markers such as synaptophysin

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathology shows small round blue cells with Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes
Pigmented lesion on iris or ciliary body

redFlags: Presence of leukocoria in a child
Secondary glaucoma with elevated intraocular pressure
references: Kaliki S, Shields CL. Medulloepithelioma of the eye. Surv Ophthalmol. 2017;62(3):333-345.
